coverage_note: 00:00-06:40 English meta talk about the verb list; 16:21-16:27 clothes answer in Latin letters (no errors: beige is on her sheet as beij); 47:49-1:03:50 mostly English rule discussion. echo: 'Ashra.' (15:44) = عشر; 15:40 'Asha' for talat-3ashar - Amal asked 'What's عشاء?' (dinner) - a dropped r, treated as S4 pronunciation, not written as a row. 06:58 ينقل unclear (engine). 10:40 بخطط -> خططت self-fix. 08:58 هادي -> هاد self-fix. 24:14 المال (MSA money) for مصاري let pass, not written. Other echo candidates are real English.

rows.medi_said: أنا سمعت / متأخر اليوم. صحيت. That's right.
rows.why: He said sami3et (I heard) for s7eet (I woke up); her صحيت at 07:06 lands inside his 07:04 line and he takes it with 'That's right' (GR-24).
Verb/noun ta2a55ar where the adjective mit2a55er is needed; her 08:35 restatement uses متأخر and he repeats it, but she gave no clear fix signal and the engine may have dropped 'mi-'.
Her whole reply is 'el' and he answers على العشرة - clock time takes el- (GR-25).
He used the he-form kaan with ana; she recasts أنا كنت and he repeats it at 08:01.

rows.amal_said: We never say هذا الصبح just say الصبح or بالصباح.
rows.why: 'This morning' is just el-subu7 (sheet: morning | el-sube7 | الصبح); he said هادي الصباح at 08:23 and again 08:54/08:58 and she ruled it out at 09:00 - one row, the first.

rows.medi_said: أنا لا مش / شجاع اليوم. مش شجاع اليوم.
rows.why: shujaa3 = brave, not motivated (sheet: motivated | Mitshajje3 | متشجع); she recasts at once.
laazem went straight to a noun; she supplies the verb 'take' in English and he says لازم أخد عطلة at 09:44 (GR-27).
rows.english: I need to take a day off.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم أخد عطلة وسفر، سفر.
rows.why: Noun safar (travel) used where the verb asaafer is needed; her English rephrase 'I should travel' and he fixes to ولازم أسافر at 09:57 (PG-22).
khattat (plan) takes la- ('plan for'); she prompts 'You plan for.' and he says لا سفر (la-safar) at 11:07.

rows.medi_said: بس أنا راح / آآآ على / عموي.
rows.amal_said: Sorry بس أنا راح what?. ... راح going. What's going؟
rows.why: He used ra7 as the verb 'go' with no verb after it; she asks 'what?' and 'What's going?' and he adds أروح at 11:52.
rows.english: But I will go to my uncle's.

rows.why: He built 3amuwi; 'my uncle' is 3am + -i = 3ammi (sheet: uncle (paternal) | 3am); she recasts twice (12:21, 12:24) and he takes it.

rows.amal_said: Either على or عند which one؟ Can't put two.
rows.why: Two prepositions stacked (3ala + 3ind; engine wrote 'and' for 3ind); she says you can't put two.

rows.medi_said: ehna rah / niru, / um... / Oh my gosh, I forgot the word for, for camping.
rows.chat: u ba3dain e7na ra7 nroo7 ta5yeem ba3ed.
rows.why: He could not find camping (sheet: camping | ta5yeem); after a خيمة hint she supplies تخييم.

rows.amal_said: Yes. بس we learned how to say الأول for a feminine. What is it?
rows.why: saa3a is feminine so the ordinal after it is el-oola; she prompts the feminine and he says الساعة الأولى at 18:31.

rows.medi_said: ساعة / تاني means the second hour, and التاني الساعة means a different hour.
rows.amal_said: لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: He put el-taani before the noun; she says it means nothing - taani goes before a bare noun or after the noun.

rows.chat: el-masari ra7 yiju fi tani youm / youm tani
rows.why: masaari is plural (she said so at 23:40) so the verb is yiju (my reading, from her chat); she only typed it, no voiced fix (GR-19).

rows.amal_said: مم، مم، هذي اليوم. / مرة، هذي المرة.
rows.chat: hadi el-marra el-tania illi bashufek elyoam
rows.why: He said el-yoam (the day) for el-marra (the time); she echoes هذي اليوم then gives المرة and he fixes at 27:27.

rows.medi_said: So ساعة الأول-- It should be ساعة الأول.
rows.chat: awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour
rows.why: Same masc ordinal after feminine saa3a again (and no el- on saa3a); she recasts twice.
Listening drill: awal el-yoam means the beginning of the day; she repeats it until he says 'The beginning of the day' at 30:52.

rows.medi_said: الأول اليوم. ... Isn't that the first day?
rows.why: He put el-awwal before el-yoam for 'the first day'; she says it means nothing and gives اليوم الأول.
Noun + el-adjective needs el- on the noun too; she recasts المرة الأخيرة and he repeats it.
He repeated her الرحلة الأخيرة without el- on the adjective; she supplies الأخيرة.

rows.medi_said: غير يوم. غير اليوم. I'll see you another day.
rows.chat: bashufek 8eir yoam = i'll see you another day
rows.why: Right after the rule 'ghair never takes el-' he said غير اليوم; she repeats غير يوم - may only be him echoing her earlier example.

rows.medi_said: هي ال، ال، الختيارة ال أول. Is it awwal?
rows.why: Feminine 5ityaara needs el-oola; she says الأولى and he swears and repeats أولى.
rows.english: She is the first old woman in our program.

rows.medi_said: Yes, uh, tan-- uh, تاني، تاني حدا. / هذا الثاني.
rows.amal_said: تاني حدا would mean the second person. ... حدا التاني is no. X. Just حدا تاني.
rows.why: For 'someone else' taani goes after the noun; before it means 'the second person'; his follow-up هذا الثاني also got 'no. X. Just حدا تاني'.

rows.amal_said: عشر y. ... y عشر not عشرة.
rows.why: 3-10 before a plural noun drop the -a ending; she says عشر not عشرة and he repeats.

rows.medi_said: الأخير، الأخيرة. ... دقيقة is masculine. So، أخ-أخير.
rows.amal_said: أخيرة. / أخيرات. [laughs] That's why I paused.
rows.why: The adjective after plural da2aaye2 is a5eeraat; he gave masc/fem singular (and called دقيقة masculine); she supplies أخيرات.

rows.chat: min aa5er muwazzafe/a / min el-muwazzafa el-a5ira
rows.why: For 'the last X' aa5er goes before a bare noun; with el- it means 'the end of X' - she asks 'The end of the employees?' and he fixes to آخر موظفة at 47:12.
rows.proposed_rule: awwal / aa5er before a noun take a bare noun for 'the first / last X'; with el- they mean 'the beginning / end of X': aa5er muwazzafe = the last employee, aa5er el-ijtima3 = the end of the meeting

rows.medi_said: غير / Uh, you say it was dwarf? What was it again?
rows.why: He asked her for the word for guests and she gave ضيوف.
rows.english: We have different guests every day.

rows.chat: ana basoo2 nafs el-taree2 kul yom
rows.why: 6ari2a = way/method, 6ari2 = road/route (sheet: road / way / route | 6ariq); she recasts and he says نفس الطريق.
rows.english: I drive the same route every day.

rows.medi_said: القانون لغير مش نفس ال-- / إشي من / نفس.
rows.why: He restarted into إشي من نفس; she prompts 'Or مش نفس...' and he says مش نفس الإشي - may be help on the way rather than a slip.
rows.english: The rule for ghair is not the same thing.
rows.proposed_rule: nafs (same) goes before the noun and the noun takes el-: nafs el-ishi, never ishi min nafs
